overview.headline: Steady glider descent linking glide angle to lift drag and weight balance

keyPoints.point: Glider is an aircraft with no engine suitable for studying aerodynamics basics
keyPoints.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.

keyPoints.point: Steady descent involves constant velocity with no acceleration while losing altitude
keyPoints.quote: If a glider is in a steady (constant velocity and no acceleration) descent, it loses altitude as it travels.

keyPoints.point: Glide angle tangent equals change in height divided by distance flown
keyPoints.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d:

keyPoints.point: Lift times sine of glide angle equals drag times cosine of glide angle
keyPoints.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: angle between flight path and ground that sets glide direction
keyTerms.quote: The flight path intersects the ground at an angle a called the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force that with drag and weight balances along glide angle
keyTerms.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W:

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic resistance along glide path that balances component of lift at given angle
keyTerms.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: downward force equal to combined lift and drag components in steady glide
keyTerms.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W:
